title: I made a Gunbound Roguelite games only using prompts and here is how I did it. Is this slop?
author: WeightNational9457
selftext:
I made a Gunbound x Worms x Roguelite in 1 week with just prompts. I've made a few games with AI and I think this is the one closest to actually being a full game and not "AI Slop". I have no real game making or dev experience, although I am in the tech industry.

Game: [https://mechbound.com/](https://mechbound.com/)

1. The game itself took 2 days before I could properly call it a full game. Then I spent 3 days polishing art, bugs, copy and balancing.

![img](hj6r5ta2uvwh1)

  
2. In the first 2 days, I started with a simple prompt before I slept - "build a gunbound rogue lite game that's AAA quality" and to my surprise it did quite well in the core mechanics e.g. shooting, aiming etc. What it didn't do well was the art, game theme (at first it was tanks) and also level progression.

![img](x2blec3etvwh1 "First output (one shot)")

3. I spent my next phase focused on building the general theme (not art) and turning it into mechs, and that allowed me to come up with more ideas on progression and art - this took around 2-3 hours.

![img](kfzwkf4btvwh1 "Old art/theme")

3. After the theme was set, I then spent some time working on art; I had many, many iterations. However, what worked for me was asking Claude to create tools for me to review artwork. I used references to Gundam (not images, I just asked it to reference Gundam SD). This took quite a while but the tool helped a lot.

![img](f3cg52m4qvwh1 "Art/Model review tool")

4. Once it looked good, it felt more fun, but the UI looked like the typical AI built games, I used a prompt along the lines of "the UI doesn't feel like it's from a game, it needs to be drawn and have game like textures" This took around 30 minutes to polish and get to 60% of what it looks like now.

![img](p9ukasrosvwh1 "Old UI")

![img](8inmfkx0tvwh1 "New UI - Output from that 1st prompt")

  
5. Next came playtesting, I played the game to completion at least 10 times. What worked for me was playing and telling Claude what I thought needed improvement so that I wouldn't forget but also I could get instant feedback in the new updates as I progressed during the game.. At this point the game is at around 80% of what you see.  


![img](u7wb2ubvtvwh1 "Sample of how I would play test")

6. Final touch-ups: I added a playground mode where I can try out individual Mods (abilities) and do final balancing and polishing. I also sent it to friends and got their reactions. This was the only game I had people actually play for more than 5 minutes.

I'm not sure what to do now. I will keep updating the game, add more levels and keep having fun with it.



Random things that helped:

1. I used Claude CLI but I mainly /remote-control when I work - I actually spend around 30-50% of my time using my phone to make changes. I prefer to use Claude desktop app to remote into the CLI because it renders screenshots and I just like the better UI.

2. Make sure you ask Claude to optimise if you feel lag or if your phone gets too hot when testing. Do this consistently or even before you sleep.

3. Ask for cool animations and badass loading screens, I really think it elevates the experience.

4. Make sure the game is playable on Mobile and vertical, I hate games that ask me to turn my phone around.

5. Ask claude to build tools, I asked it to build a tool to make the game trailer - I didn't spend too much time on it and I probably should have.

![img](p1f0nyrgxvwh1 "Trailer tool - Could have been better")

TDLR  
I made a game that I don't think is AI slop, here is my process and I learn't a lot and had fun.

comments.author: tomato-shadow
comments.body:
Yes it's slop.

Glad you learned and had fun.

Looks good, obviously based on a lot of similar games. 
Not the worst thing, but might have to keep bug fixing and prompting

comments.body: It looks fun but a bit uninspired. It doesn’t look like you spent muck time iterating on the art style.

comments.body: Looks cool, ignore the haters, they've never made anything.

comments.body: A forgettable replication (with typical AI flaws) of a good game also falls under AI slop.
